prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five downward-angled workshop frames, the depth map shows the camera wearer's own torso and arms in the lower foreground at 0.2 to 0.6 metres (brightest white), while no other people are present in the scene. In frames 1 and 2, a cluttered metal workbench with a vice and a plastic jug sits directly in front and to the left at roughly 0.7 to 1.2 metres (within arm's reach) above the dark floor at 1.5 to 2.0 metres; in frames 3 and 4, the wearer turns clockwise and steps away from the bench past a motorcycle front wheel on the left, a red floor ramp in front (1.5–2.0 m), and cylindrical bins along the right wall (0.8–1.4 m) before approaching a workbench and overhead blue tool pegboard in frame 5 where the wearer's extended left hand reaches a hanging wrench at about 0.5 to 0.7 metres beside a wall calendar at 0.4 metres on the upper left. The depth map clarifies the 3D elevation of the tables, containers, and right wall relative to the flat floor, which is hard to judge from the cluttered overhead RGB textures alone, and shows how the wearer's body and extended arm occlude the floor and lower table edges beneath them. However, the depth map is unreliable in frames 4 and 5 where the upper-right wall and pegboard are overexposed as bright white (falsely indicating nearness closer than 0.5 m), and it blurs thin tools on the workbench and pegboard into flat planes.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects no other people in the workshop and only partially captures the camera wearer's own downward-facing body (0.2–0.7 m from the camera) and a single object across the five-frame turn from the first workbench to the second workbench. It segments the wearer's lower-left red jacket torso in frame 1, misses the wearer completely in frames 2 and 4, merges the wearer's right arm with the cylindrical grey floor bin and hose on the right (0.8–1.2 m away) in frame 3, and isolates the extended left arm reaching up to the pegboard tools (0.4–0.7 m away, within arm's reach) in frame 5. While it cleanly separates the boundary of the wearer's raised left sleeve and gloved hand against the busy tool pegboard in frame 5—a contour that is visually cluttered in the RGB—it fails to segment any of the workbenches, tools, motorcycle parts, or floor ramps that lie 0.5 to 2.0 metres away. The map is highly unreliable overall: in frame 2 it misclassifies the light-blue plastic jug on the upper-right corner of the workbench (about 1.0 m away and 0.8 m from the left-side tool rack) as a 'bird', in frame 3 it bleeds the 'person' mask onto the adjacent trash bin, and in frame 5 it outputs duplicate overlapping 'person' labels for the single left arm while cutting off the rest of the wearer's torso at the bottom edge.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1 through 4, detecting neither the camera wearer's self-occluded, downward-viewed torso and arms (0.2–0.6 m from the lens) nor any other person as the wearer turns clockwise through the workshop from the first workbench toward the pegboard wall. In frame 5, it outputs a single yellow body skeleton over the wearer's extended left arm (0.3–0.7 m away, upper-left to centre-left) as it reaches within arm's reach to grasp a vertical wrench on the pegboard about 0.6 metres in front of the wearer. Rather than mapping the arm's true anatomical joints, this skeleton is an unreliable false-positive configuration that hallucinates a miniature full-body stick figure—complete with a clustered head/face keypoint group near the orange-gloved hand and hip/leg segments running down the red sleeve—facing right and slightly away from the camera. Because magenta hand keypoints are completely absent in all five frames and the heavy top-down perspective cuts off the wearer's head and shoulders behind the lens, the pose map contributes no reliable spatial information beyond confirming the 2D location and upward diagonal axis of the reaching left arm in frame 5.
